title: What is known about 1RB1LA_0LC0RE_1LD1LB_1RE1LF_1RC0RA_0RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LA_0LC0RE_1LD1LB_1RE1LF_1RC0RA_0RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is a base-4 counter of walls in a sea of 100, incremented from the right end. Lean proves one sweep for every carry chain (any length) for every edge event seen: the overflow, four kinds of merger and seven left-end cases; an exact digit simulator, checked against the direct run, ran to 2.2·1015 steps without a halt or an unknown event. No closed set of digit configurations has been found: the safe mergers depend on a mod-4 relation between neighbouring digits.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 64,212 cells have been visited and 26,731 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.064). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.539).

claims.title: The shift rules
claims.text: Going right, E turns (101)<sup>n</sup> and (011)<sup>n</sup> into (010)<sup>n</sup>, A turns (011)<sup>n</sup> into (100)<sup>n</sup>, B turns (110)<sup>n</sup> into (001)<sup>n</sup>; going left, D turns (100)<sup>n</sup> back into (101)<sup>n</sup>, B and C rewrite (010)<sup>n</sup> and (001)<sup>n</sup>, A runs over 1s. Each for every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: One sweep adds one, for a carry chain of any length
claims.text: At the sample point (C on a 0 at the right end) the tape is a list of digits (100)^r W. With the first non-S3 digit (the stop) in shape S0, S1 or S2 and any list ts of S3 digits after it (any length, any runs), one sweep turns the stop into the next shape (S0→S1, S1→S2 with its left run one shorter, S2→S3), every S3 of the chain into S0, and lengthens the last run by one. Proved by induction on the list (seqtm).

claims.title: The overflow, the mergers and the left end
claims.text: 0^inf 10 followed only by S3 digits (any number): one sweep crosses the whole tape, every S3 becomes S0 and a new digit S1 is born at the right end (overflow). An S1 with left run 0 receiving a carry fuses with the wall before it: after S into one S0 (merge_s_s1), after S3 into S and S0 (merge_s3_s1), after S2 into X6 = 1000000 (merge_s2_s1); X6 and X5 as stops (sweep_x6, sweep_x5). At the left end, eight cases with a first digit of run 0 (left_s_s1, left_s0, left_s1, left_s2, left_s3, left_s_s0, left_s_s2, left_s3_s). Each for any carry chain.

claims.title: The digit model is exact
claims.text: py/digits.py maps one sample to the next by running the machine symbolically (symtm) on a window (the carry chain, the stop, and as many digits before it as the run touches; the rest an unknown context; long runs as variables). Compared with the direct run from blank tape: the same tapes and the same step counts at all 14,148 sample points up to 2·108 steps.

claims.title: No halt in 2.2·10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: From the sample at 2·109 steps the digit model ran 4.9·107 sweeps more, to 2.2·1015 steps: no halt and no window it could not read back as digits; overflows and mergers as described, the first block went from 14 down to 0 (one per overflow) near 2.1·1015 steps, the left end rearranged ([0]S3 [0]S [436]S0 → [0]S [0]S0 [435]S0) and the counter went on.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.77×10<sup>19</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 17,748,289,296,345,434,315 without a halt. At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,017,009 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Why it probably never halts
claims.text: Every event seen is one of a small catalogue of local rewrites of digits, each a Lean rule, none of which reaches F on a 1. The dangerous mergers (an S1 of run 0 after S0 or S1, which would leave the vocabulary) never occur, because of a mod-4 relation: for neighbouring digits y x, phase(y) + run(x) + [x is S2 or S3] mod 4 is fixed while both live, and is 2 or 3 in 2,091,564 of 2,092,788 neighbour pairs over the first 3·10<sup>5</sup> sweeps (the rest inside S[0]S0 compounds).

claims.title: No small closed language
claims.text: The fixpoint search py/closure.py ngram (every place a sweep can happen in a word of the language, run symbolically) does not close for bigrams or trigrams with run classes 0, 1, ≥2, nor for bigrams with residues mod 4, a marked left end and the compounds S[0]S0, S[0]S1 (536 bigrams, then windows with X5 or X6 before an S1 of run 0, which the real run never shows).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Missing: a closed set of digit configurations. n-gram languages over (wall, run class), with classes 0/1/≥2 or with residues mod 4, compounds and a marked left end, all fail to close in py/closure.py, and cell-level closed tape languages (windows of 3..7 cells, block trackers) do not close within 4·105 abstract configurations. Also missing: carry chains with an S3 of run 0 in seqtm, and the assembly in Lean.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine counts in base 4: its tape is a sea of the word 100 with walls in it, each wall a digit, and every trip of the head from the right end adds one. The gaps between the walls slowly close, walls merge, and when every digit reads 3 the counter overflows and a new digit is born. This page shows how, with the rules proved in Lean.

facts.text: No halt in the exact digit simulator.
Every edge event seen, proved in Lean for carry chains of any length.
How fast the gap in front of a wall shrinks: walls merge.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: A sea of 100 with digits in it
html: Look at the tape each time the head is at the right end in state C, reading a 0. It is the word 100 repeated, interrupted by short walls; each wall with the run of 100 in front of it is one digit:

A real tape (step 1,999,995,206), each digit written [run]wall: [0]S [14]S1 [490]S0 [922]S1 [1642]S0 [427]S0 [5933]S2 [15297]S0 [4360]. S is the 10 at the left end; the last number is the run at the right end, one word longer after every trip of the head.

sections.heading: Adding one
html: From the right end the head walks left over the digits that read 3 (S3) — the carry chain — to the first digit that does not, moves it one step along S0→S1→S2→S3, and walks back turning every S3 into S0: adding one to a base-4 number whose lowest digit is next to the head. The head passes the k-th digit only once every 4k trips, so most trips are short.

Example: [a+1]S1 [c+1]S3 [d+1]S3 [z+1] becomes [a]S2 [c+1]S0 [d+1]S0 [z+2]. Lean proves each such rule for every value of the runs and a carry chain of any length, by induction on the list (sweep_s0, sweep_s1, sweep_s2).

Only the S1→S2 step changes a run: the run in front of the digit loses one word. So the gap in front of every wall shrinks by one per cycle of that wall. Between two overflows the i-th digit from the left goes round 4i−1 times, which is what the first look at this machine saw: block i loses 4i−1 between visits of the left end.

sections.heading: Overflows and mergers
html: Overflow. When every digit reads 3, the head runs to the left end: every S3 becomes S0 and a new digit S1 is born at the right end, the old last run in front of it (overflow, proved for any number of digits). At step 3,364,427,683 the tape was [0]S [13]S0 [487]S0 [910]S0 [1595]S0 [239]S0 [5182]S0 [12291]S0 [16383]S1 [1]. These overflows are the rare visits of the left end, about four times further apart each time.

Merger. When the gap in front of an S1 is used up, the next carry cannot shorten it, and the S1 fuses with the wall before it: after S the two become one S0 (merge_s_s1), after S3 they become S and S0 (merge_s3_s1), after S2 a long wall X6 = 1000000 (merge_s2_s1), which the next carry splits again (sweep_x6). After S0 or S1 it would make walls outside the list; that never happens in the run, because of a mod-4 relation between a digit's phase and its neighbour's run (see the README).

The first block. The gap behind the leading 10 loses one word per overflow; when it is gone, 10 110 becomes 1000 (left_s_s1). The seven other ways the left end was seen to look are Lean theorems too (left_s0 … left_s3_s): none halts, all come back to the digit form.

sections.heading: Only by F reading a 1
html: The only halt is state F reading a 1. None of the rules above gets there. A simulator that applies them (each an actual symbolic run of the machine, not a model) matched the real run at every sample point checked and ran on to 2.2·1015 steps without a halt or an unknown event.

To make that a proof one has to describe a set of digit configurations that the rules map into itself, including every way a short gap can sit next to every wall, and check it in Lean. The rules for every event seen are done, for any length of carry chain; the closed set is not: simple descriptions (which wall may follow which, with gap lengths 0, 1 or more, or gap lengths mod 4) all let in configurations the machine never reaches, and those leave the list of walls.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.064). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.539).
After 109 steps the tape spans 64,212 cells (51 left of the start, 44,132 right), with a density of 1s of 0.416.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A base-4 counter of walls in a sea of 100, incremented from the right end: one sweep turns the trailing S3 digits into S0 and steps the next digit; each digit's left run shrinks by one per cycle, so walls merge, and an overflow turns every digit to S0 and adds one; every edge event seen is a Lean rule for any carry chain, but no closed language is known.
